description: Each panel shows a grid with five rows and six columns. Rows are numbered from top to bottom and columns from left to right, both starting at 1. On the left, the array stores 1, 3, 2, 5, 4 consecutively in the first five cells of row 2. On the right, the linked list nodes are scattered throughout the grid. Each node occupies two adjacent cells, one for the value and one for the pointer.
Light gray cells indicate available space. Array cells are green, linked list value cells are teal, and pointer cells are light blue. The table below lists the nodes' positions in traversal order.

frames.explanation: Adjacent positions give an array its order, while a linked list is traversed by following successor pointers. Although node 4 appears at the top, it comes last in 1 → 3 → 2 → 5 → 4. Its pointer value is unspecified. Contiguous storage needs no separate successor pointer for each element. Scattered nodes can use fragments of free space but require extra storage for pointers.
frames.title: Memory layouts of arrays and linked lists

summary: The same logical sequence can occupy contiguous storage or be linked by pointers between scattered nodes.
